records.inspection_scope: Original or index archived; substantive review depth separately recorded.
records.reviewed_coverage: Entire substantive dated ICBA statement, contextual introduction and institutional description. Site navigation/related-article links excluded.
records.finding: Rebeca Romero Rainey urges Congress to strengthen the yield prohibition to prevent evasion. The stated chain is that remuneration draws retail deposits from community banks into less-protected stablecoins, inhibiting lending, increasing borrowing costs and reducing credit. Separate paragraphs resist nonbank Federal Reserve accounts/reserves, wider issuer activities, and commerce/banking integration.
records.limitations: A public advocacy release, not a consultation submission. It documents pre-enactment strengthening advocacy after a prohibition had already entered legislative debate; it does not establish the origin of the ban or causal influence. No separate reserve-income-pass-through position is assigned.
records.quantitative_action: No change to frozen respondent-level dataset, counts or heatmap.
records.short_exact_excerpt: Congress should strengthen the prohibition on yield-bearing stablecoins to ensure the intent of the legislation cannot be evaded.

records.manuscript_implication: Optional dated illustration of pre-enactment bank-credit advocacy; preserve channel distinction and do not claim this originated the restriction.

records.document_title: OCC Implementing GENIUS Act NPR RIA FINAL OIRA
records.actor: OCC Implementing GENIUS Act NPR RIA FINAL OIRA
records.inspection_scope: Full original RIA archived; substantive semantic review remains pending.
records.reviewed_coverage: All 24 PDF pages, including footnotes, cost components, alternatives and nonquantified effects.
records.finding: This proposed-rule regulatory impact assessment expressly assumes the issuer ban and presumed affiliate/related-third-party restriction (p.7). Its evaluated alternatives concern capital and operating-expense backstops (pp.21–22), not paying versus forbidding holder remuneration. Its $1.72 million estimated 2026 net issuer cost saving relates to the entire proposed regime and selected baselines, not the welfare benefit of the remuneration ban. Treasury-demand/short-term-credit effects (pp.19–21) and nonquantified consumer/producer surplus (pp.23–24) likewise address the proposed regime as a whole.
records.limitations: The title FINAL OIRA denotes the submitted impact-assessment file, not an adopted final regulation. This finding establishes the scope of this assessment; it does not prove that no economic argument exists elsewhere or that the agency had discretion to repeal the statutory ban.
records.quantitative_action: No change to frozen respondent-level dataset, counts or heatmap.
records.document_date_note: 2026 proposal; first page gives planned February 2026 action, not a verified day.
records.short_exact_excerpt: this analysis assumes that PPSIs will not pay the holder of a payment stablecoin any form of interest or yield
records.manuscript_implication: Useful narrowly worded evidence: the OCC economic assessment takes non-remuneration as a premise instead of separately testing its marginal costs and benefits.

records.document_title: GENIUS Act Broad-Based Principles for Determining Whether a State-level Regulatory Regime Is Substantially Similar to the Federal Regulatory Framework
records.reviewed_coverage: PDF pp.1–2 (status/scope), 51–54 (additional activities and ban explanation), 84 (proposed operative provision), 87 (classification table); full extracted text searched to locate remuneration passages.
records.finding: The proposed state-regime equivalence framework requires state-qualified issuers to observe statutory prohibitions, including interest/yield (proposed section 1521.4(h)(3), PDF p.84; explanation p.53). The p.87 table classifies the interest prohibition as uniform while other provisions allow state calibration. This confirms federal/state propagation of the statutory boundary; it supplies no separate economic defense in the examined passages.
records.limitations: Prepublication NPRM with placeholders and a warning that the Federal Register version is official. Do not cite as an adopted final rule or infer a full-document negative. The remaining non-remuneration sections have not been read semantically.
records.quantitative_action: No change to frozen respondent-level dataset, counts or heatmap.
records.document_date_note: 2026 prepublication proposal; exact publication date not inferred from undated first-page placeholders.
records.manuscript_implication: Usually unnecessary for argument findings; use only if describing the proposed federal/state scope.

records.inspection_scope: Original or index archived; substantive review depth separately recorded.
records.reviewed_coverage: Compilation PDF pp.3–5 (contents/identity) and 92–94 (printed pp.88–90: complete Sherman–Massad exchange with surrounding discussion); full 18-page Massad prepared statement separately recovered/read. Native text screened across compilation, not treated as substantive whole-document review.
records.finding: In the February 11, 2025 hearing, Timothy Massad opposes treating stablecoins as interest-paying investments, qualifying this as an initial policy choice when challenged. His prepared statement (p.10) explains the concern more fully: proposed securities-law exclusion removes an existing interest-payment disincentive and could allow money-market-like products under fifty separate state regimes; he asks Congress either to prohibit interest or empower regulators to do so. Sherman challenges stablecoin utility versus regulated remunerated money-market funds, but his questions are not coded as an affirmative permission position.
records.limitations: The 215-page compilation is incomplete in native extraction: 158 pages contain fewer than 100 extracted characters, often only printed page numbers. These scanned appendices and written contributions were not silently treated as irrelevant. Massad’s full original was recovered to overcome the relevant gap; other contributions and appendices remain incompletely reviewed. The hearing exchange alone does not support a permanent universal prohibition stance.
records.quantitative_action: No change to frozen respondent-level dataset, counts or heatmap.

actor_mapping.status: No matching Massad actor row found in the frozen respondent-level dataset. New qualitative supplement only; personal views, not Harvard institutional position.

records.manuscript_implication: Add as a named nonbank restriction argument if space allows: legal classification and fragmented prudential oversight, combined with payments-versus-investment and a precautionary initial approach. Do not assign reserve-income-pass-through opposition from a general interest ban.

recovered_full_document.coverage: All 18 pages, including footnotes. Entire stablecoin section pp.2–11 read, alongside market-structure, crypto-stockpile, CBDC and memecoin sections.
recovered_full_document.pinpoint: p.10, No Prohibition on Payment of Interest; compare hearing printed p.89/PDF93.
recovered_full_document.short_exact_excerpt: We should either prohibit the payment of interest or at least empower regulators to do so.
recovered_full_document.finding: Explicit restriction/delegated restriction recommendation, motivated by payment/investment distinction and securities-law/state-supervision concerns. General support for safe reserve assets does not specify who should receive reserve earnings. Source says personal views, not Harvard Kennedy School views (p.1).
recovered_full_document.quantitative_action: No new row or count. Supplement only.

methods_wording: A supplementary pass examined seven remaining locally available US source records. It read three complete substantive documents, inspected two metadata/index pages, and reviewed relevant passages in two longer records. It also recovered and read the complete eighteen-page prepared statement of a hearing witness where the compiled record’s native text omitted the scanned contribution. These checks supplemented qualitative interpretation; they did not alter the frozen actor–episode cohort or figure. Targeted review and index inspection were not counted as complete substantive-document review.
